messages:
Fiona (PM): Quick sync 10m: we need to lock the MVP cutlist and milestone for the public launch. Two risky items on the table: predictive routing (runtime request steering) and dynamic quantization (on-the-fly model quant). Both are valuable but increase blast radius. Recommend we carve them to v1 and keep deterministic batching + conservative caching for MVP. Opinions?
Arjun (Eng): Agree. Predictive routing adds stateful routing tables and fallback complexity. Dynamic quant requires runtime kernel negotiation and a lot of QA. Both could cause opaque errors in production.
Maya (SRE): Ops note: predictive routing changes the routing path and will complicate autoscaler heuristics. If we ship it for MVP we risk cross-tenant noise and scaling thrash. Recommend pilot-only behind tenant flags.
Zane (Design): UX impact: predictive routing is not customer-visible initially, but if toggled it can change performance characteristics. We should show a small "Experimental pilot feature " in Console for any tenant with it enabled.
Hannah (Sales): A couple of prospects want cost savings from quantization. They said they'd take a paid pilot. If we gate quantization behind pilot flags it's fine. Need clear timeline for pilot enablement.
Fiona (PM): Decision proposal: public MVP ships WITHOUT predictive routing and WITHOUT dynamic quant. Ship conservative embedding-cache improvements and batching optimizations. Expose both predictive routing and dynamic quant as invite-only pilot features for Dedicated and private customers via feature flags.
Arjun (Eng): Implementation notes: 
- Add per-tenant feature flags for predictive-routing and dynamic-quant (API + Console exposure).
- Keep routing policy deterministic for public-mvp branch.
- Quant path stays in a separate feature branch with CI gating.
I estimate ~4 dev-days to add flags + 2d for Console flag UI wiring.
Maya (SRE): Canary plan: pilot flags enabled only on dedicated pools. For any pilot rollout, run a 72h canary at 2 tenants, monitor p95, queue depth, and error-rates. If p95 increases >15% revert flag. Ops will need a runbook.
Zane (Design): I'll prepare the Console tag and a small helptooltip copy: "Experimental pilot feature ". Also a tenant settings CTA: "Request pilot access".
Hannah (Sales): Timeline ask: pilots want quant enabled within 10 business days of flag availability. SE onboarding doc required.
Fiona (PM): Action items: 
- Fiona: update roadmap snapshot + public MVP one-pager to reflect cuts (EOD).
- Arjun: feature-flag PR + routing determinism revert for public branch (PR by Tue).
- Maya: canary/rollback runbook template and dashboards (post-PR).
- Zane: Console tag + tooltip copy (tomorrow).
- Hannah: notify pilot customers and collect acceptance; compile pilot list (by Fri).
ops-bot: Canary guard: global rollout blocked until canary p95 < 320ms in primary regions.
Fiona (PM): We'll reconvene Fri 9am to check PR status, canary readiness, and pilot commitments. If a prospect is a clear revenue trigger and demands an MVP exception, escalate to execs for an exception review.
Arjun (Eng): I'll post PR link here when ready and include a short performance appendix to show expected delta.
Maya (SRE): I'll slot the canary window and add alert thresholds to the dashboard.
Zane (Design): Adding the UI mocks to the shared drive and will link here.
Hannah (Sales): I'll start outreach this afternoon.
Fiona (PM): Thanks team 60; keeping MVP tight preserves launch reliability while preserving pilot revenue paths. :white_check_mark:
